title: Introduce client cancel + stale-lease probe with tool reentrancy safeguards (OpenAI-compat)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: production customers see a class of user-visible failures when clients abruptly cancel or disconnect during long tool/formatted calls. The server may hold a lease and the inflight toolcall can be replayed or double-executed after a client reconnect. This PR implements a lightweight stale-lease probe + tightened cancel semantics to reduce double-execution risk while preserving resumability for benign reconnects.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a server-initiated stale-lease probe that differentiates abandoned sessions from short reconnect windows. The probe escalates timeouts conservatively before reclaiming KV/lease resources.
- Introduces a client-cancel token update path: clients can send a final-cancel marker which causes the server to tombstone the stream but preserve a resumable checkpoint for a short grace window.
- Adds tool-call reentrancy metadata and dedupe checks (idempotency-by-tool-call-id) for tool integrations invoked during streaming. Tool plugins opt into the check via a small SDK surface.
- Updates the OpenAI-compat adapter to map cancel semantics and expose the new probe/tombstone events over the streaming protocol.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Probe behavior favors availability: we lengthen the reclaim window by default (configurable) to avoid reclaiming during typical client reconnects (cellular/mobile). Operators can tighten this via the session.expiry_policy config.
- Idempotency is best-effort: tools must provide deterministic ids or be marked non-reentrant. For legacy tool integrations we fall back to at-most-once best-effort with explicit audit logs.
- No user-facing breaking changes to existing OpenAI-compat clients: old clients will see the same streaming messages, but will not emit the new cancel marker. They continue to be protected by the extended probe window.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated behind runtime flag stream.stale_lease_probe (off in canary).
2) Canary (10% traffic) with canary-specific probe windows and additional metrics.
3) 100% rollout after 48h of canary with no increase in tool double-execution alerts.

Testing:
- Unit tests for session manager, probe state machine, and idempotency table in go/service/session_manager_test.go.
- Integration test that simulates client disconnect -> reconnect within window and ensures no duplicated tool calls.
- Load tests replicate long-running tool calls with random client disconnects to validate latency/cost impact.
- Local sharp-failure test to reproduce early abort and ensure tombstone path cleans up correctly.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the probe state machine minimal (three states: active, probed, tombstoned) to avoid long-lived orchestration logic. Future follow-ups will add observability dashboards and per-tenant tuning UI.

summary_of_changes: Server: stale-lease probe and tombstone transition; Session manager adds client_cancel_marker and conservative reclaim. Adapter: OpenAI streaming mapping for new events. Tools SDK: reentrancy id header and dedupe table. Tests/docs/helm updates and rollout guide added.
notes_for_backport: Non-breaking behavior, but operators running <= v1.8 must upgrade session manager and adapter together. Backport candidate for 1.9.x if customers request reduced double-exec risk for tool integrations.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: if tombstone window is too short, clients on flaky networks may see increased aborted sessions. Mitigation: conservative defaults, feature flag gating, and per-tenant runtime tuning. Added canary dashboard and automated rollback on error-rate spikes.
